reconcile.note: Gill reads Psalm 22's hiding of God's face as only for a moment, with the same psalm affirming the cry was heard, so hiding texts mean temporary withdrawal, not reliable absence.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll presses history's persecuted victims against the psalm's promise that God hears and answers those who call on him in trouble.

quotes.text: Can all the agonies and crimes, can all the inequalities of the world be answered by reading the "noble Psalm" in which are found the words: "Call upon me in the day of trouble, so I will hear thee, and thou shalt praise me"? Do you prove the truth of these fine words, this honey of Trebizond, by the victims of religious persecution?
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III (1881), on Psalm 46:1.

sides.snippet: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? Why are you so far from helping me, and from the words of my groaning?
